location: North York Central Library (Toronto Public Library)

Though Ladino is disappearing from daily use, the spirit of its rich, oral tradition remains. Drop by a branch with a Youth Hub or call the branch to find out more.

title: Crafting Social Circle
location: Oakwood Village Library and Arts Centre (Toronto Public Library)
description: Do you like to crochet, embroider, knit, sew, or something else entirely? If you are looking to chat with some fellow crafters while enjoying your favourite hobby, come join our Crafting Circle! Bring your own supplies and a small project. All skill levels welcome.

title: Finding Recovery Through Exercise Skills and Hope (FRESH)
description: This program helps people stay active, make friends, learn new skills, and have fun. It involves peer-led group activities which can include crafts, games, walking, yoga, and more. Meet new folks, build social connections, and tell us about programs and services you would like to see in the neighbourhood! On Tuesdays, join us for crafts (11am-1pm) a walk (11:15am-1pm) chair yoga (11:30am-12:30pm), and music wellness (1-2pm). Snacks and refreshments are provided for all participants. Ingredient lists will be available at the program. This program is in collaboration with Gerstein Crisis Centre'

title: Housing Help
description: Drop in and work one-on-one with staff from The Housing Help Centre (THHC) to determine your housing needs, connect you to other government services, and to match you with landlords across the city. THHC works with both individuals and families in the City of Toronto to find and maintain affordable, safe housing. THHC can be contacted at 416-285-8070.

title: Newcomer Settlement Services
description: New to Canada? Need information on employment, housing, language learning, schools, or other topics? A Settlement Worker can help. Drop in to meet our settlement worker every Tuesday afternoon from 2 pm-5 pm. Visit our branch or contact Ada Tao at 416-770-0312 or atao@cathcrosscultural.org. In partnership with Catholic Crosscultural Services. Please bring your immigration documents (PR card) with you

title: Finding Recovery Through Exercise Skills and Hope (FRESH): Movie or Walk Tuesdays
description: This program helps people stay active, make friends, learn new skills, and have fun. Meet new folks, build connections, and tell us about programs and services you would like to see in the neighbourhood! A feature film will be shown every Tuesday. Connect with others and watch something new, or revisit an old favourite in a safe and friendly setting. Participants can also connect on a neighbourhood walk with a F.R.E.S.H. peer. Drop-in, all are welcome. Snacks and refreshments are provided for all participants. Ingredient lists will be available at the program. This program is in collaboration

title: Youth Hub: Board Game Café
description: Join us in the Youth Hub every Tuesday to play board games with your friends! Ask us for our list of board games, and check our monthly calendar for Tournaments with prizes! All materials provided. This program is part of Youth Hub service. Youth Hubs are a welcoming place for teens after school and in the summer, where helpful staff are always available. Free, nutritious snacks are offered daily. Drop by a branch with a Youth Hub or call the branch to find out more.

title: Community Writing Workshop
description: Experience the transformative power of writing in an inclusive space! A Writers Collective of Canada (WCC) workshop is unlike any other. We write together, share first drafts in an encouraging environment, listen deeply to one another, and receive supportive feedback. Tap into your story and explore your voice in an environment of dignity, courage, and respect. No experience required. Beginners are welcome. Materials are provided.

title: Play, Stretch & Connect
description: Join us for a fun and social game of BINGO designed for seniors! It’s a great way to stay mentally sharp and body active, connecting with others in a friendly, relaxed atmosphere. Prizes, laughter, and good company await!

title: Finding Recovery Through Exercise Skills and Hope (FRESH): Music Wellness
description: This program helps people stay active, make friends, learn new skills, and have fun. Meet new folks, build connections, and tell us about programs and services you would like to see in the neighbourhood! Join us and make some music! Express your creativity, explore a variety of instruments, and sing your favourite songs. Connect with others and have fun! No musical training or experience needed. Drop-in, all are welcome. Call 416-393-7653 for more info. Snacks and refreshments are provided for all participants at 3:30 pm. Ingredient lists will be available at the program. This program is in co

title: Woolly Wednesdays
description: Yearning for yarn? Join our afternoon needlecraft circle! Whether you are a seasoned crochetier or picking up a set of knitting needles for the first time, everyone is welcome to share techniques, enjoy friendly conversation, and learn a new skill. Connect with fellow craftspeople as you work on your project. We will have some supplies available for beginners, but please feel free to bring your own. Drop-in; no registration required.

THHC works with both individuals and families in the City of Toronto to find and maintain affordable, safe housing. The Housing Help Centre can be contacted at 416-285-8070 or at shhc.ca.

title: Knit Wits Knitting and Crochet Club
description: Main Street's knitting and crochet club returns! Share your projects with other knitters/crocheters, teach a technique, learn a technique, and enjoy great conversation. All level of knitters/crocheters welcome. Bring your own yarn, needles, and crochet hooks. We meet on the second floor of the library. Drop-in program.

title: Needleworx
description: Bring your own knitting or crocheting project, or start something new while enjoying relaxed conversation! All are welcome! This is a drop in program. No registration request.

title: New Year’s Eve
address: 100 Queen St W, Toronto, ON M5H 2N2
description: New Year’s Eve at Nathan Phillips Square

Snacks and refreshments are provided for all participants. Ingredient lists will be available at the program. This program is in collaboration with Gerstein Crisis Centre's F.R.E.S.H. initiative .

title: Cinema Italiano
description: Join fellow Italian Cinema lovers. Classic and contemporary films from various genres will be screened each month (with English subtitles).

title: Family Time
description: Join us for stories, songs, rhymes and activities in this program for children ages 5 and under and their parents or caregivers. Family Time runs from 11 to 11:30. Children, parents, and caregivers are invited to join us for a fun craft from 11:30 to 12:00.

title: Lego Free Play
description: LEGO Free Play is a fun, creative program where children can build anything they imagine using LEGO bricks. There are no instructions or rules to follow, kids are free to explore, create, and play at their own pace. This open-ended play encourages creativity, problem-solving, and social interaction. Drop-in program, no registration required.

title: Lego Builders Club
description: LEGO Builders Club is a fun, STEAM based program where children can build anything they imagine using LEGO bricks. Kids are free to explore, create, and play at their own pace, encouraging creativity, problem-solving, and social interaction. Drop-in program, no registration required.

title: Sunday SNAP Circuits
description: Come join us and explore electricity and circuitry. Learn about circuits and gain hands on experience with SNAP Circuits! Feel the spark when you build your own circuit! For children ages 6-12. Drop in.

title: Curious Chaos Club
description: Step into The Curious Chaos Club- where creativity gets a little messy (in the best way!) Kids ages 6- 12 can build, create and let the chaos begin!

title: STEM Sundays
description: Drop-in each Sunday and explore various arts and crafts, building materials and technologies.

title: Sunday STEAM at the Riverdale Branch
description: Join us for a fun STEAM program on Sunday afternoon! Programs cycle between Robotics, Snap Circuits, LEGO, K'nex, Marble Run and Kids Craft Club. For Children ages 5 and up. Drop-in.

title: Sunday Family Club
description: Enjoy and have fun on Sunday afternoons at Guildwood Library! Will you colour your favourite characters, do a craft or show off your building skills with LEGO and KEVA? Maybe it will be Snap Circuits or Board Games? Every Sunday come in for a surprise!

title: STEAM Lab
description: Join us for our weekly STEAM Lab (Ages 6-12) , where kids can explore science, technology, engineering, art, and math through fun, hands-on activities. From building simple robots and experimenting with Snap Circuits to creative design challenges and more, there’s always something new to discover. Activities change each week, so there’s always something new to explore!

title: Family Time
description: Join us for stories, songs, rhymes and activities in this program for children ages 5 and under and their parents or caregivers. Family Time runs from 2pm to 2:30pm .

title: Sunday Tech Time
description: Explore the world of circuitry and robots. Test out Snap Circuits, Dash robots, or Spheros. Ages 5 and up.

title: Family Storytime
description: Join us for stories, songs, rhymes and activities in this program for children ages 5 and under and their parents or caregivers. Family Storytime runs from 2-2:30pm. Drop in. No registration required but space is limited.

title: Sunday Funday
description: Join us for a fun afternoon of video games, board games, Lego and ping pong. Drop in, no registration required. Recommended for ages 6-12.

title: Movies From Around the World
description: Join us every second Monday of the month (unless specified otherwise) as we bring the world to you through the power of cinema! Beginning with a small introduction, we will be hosting screenings from various movies from around the world, so we hope to see you there! title: Common Misconceptions About Investing
location: North York Central Library (Toronto Public Library)
description: Presented by Riverdale Immigrant Women’s Centre (RIWC) , this workshop helps to address myths about investing and introduces simple, beginner-friendly investment concepts only. Registration encouraged. Drop-ins are welcome until capacity is reached.

description: Presented by Riverdale Immigrant Women's Centre , this workshop helps to address myths about investing and introduces simple, beginner-friendly investment concepts only. Drop in.

description: Calling all children ages 9 to 12 and their mother, father, grandmother, grandfather, or caregiver! Join our monthly family book club. One child 9 to 12, one parent/caregiver, one book per month. Last Monday of every month, unless noted otherwise. First meeting is on Monday August 31. Registration is required. title: Resilience Reads: a climate neighbourhood reading party
description: Join us to share the joy of reading, while building climate resilience knowledge. Members are invited to discuss a book they are reading, tell stories, and empower each other to explore community-driven solutions. Each party will start with a quiet read and reflect time, with opportunities to join group discussions later on over refreshments. MAY – All women are water defenders Memory of Water by Emmi Itaranta or your favourite book featuring water! JUNE – Righting our relationship with land Earth Keeper by N. Scott Momaday or your favourite book that shares how words are medicine! JULY – Clim

title: Robotics Workshops for Youth
description: Join Upper Toronto Community Robotics for accessible, hands-on robotics and engineering workshops for youth! These programs will help you build foundational skills in engineering design, safety, CAD software, 3D modeling, and introductory robotics coding. This program is for youth in grades 6-12. It is highly recommended to attend each session to build on your learning. Please register online.
